subject: science
chapter_title: Cell: The Building Block of Life

concepts.title: The Cell as the Unit of Life
concepts.definition: All living beings are organised from cells - single-celled organisms carry out life with one cell, while plants, fish, birds and humans are built of millions of cells working together; a group of similar cells performing a similar job forms a tissue, the next level of organisation.
concepts.key_idea: Cell to tissue to organism: life is architecture built from cellular bricks.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc102.txt opening and cell sections (unicellular, multicellular, tissues)
question_patterns: why is the cell called the building block of life
differentiate unicellular and multicellular organisms with examples
what is a tissue and how does it arise from cells
give two examples of single-celled organisms
arrange cell, tissue, organ and organism in order of complexity

solution_steps.explain: The cell is the smallest structure showing all life processes.
One cell runs an amoeba; millions of specialised cells build a human.
Similar cells combine into tissues, tissues into organs and systems.

concepts.title: Cell Structure: Membrane, Nucleus and Organelles
concepts.definition: A cell is bounded by a plasma membrane that controls entry and exit, with a gel-like cytoplasm holding organelles; the nucleus stores genetic material and directs the cell, while mitochondria, ribosomes and other organelles divide the labour of life.
concepts.key_idea: Membrane guards, nucleus commands, organelles work - a cell is a miniature factory.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc102.txt cell structure sections (membrane, nucleus, organelles)
question_patterns: draw and label the main parts of a cell
what is the function of the plasma membrane
why is the nucleus called the control centre of the cell
name three cell organelles and their functions
which organelle releases energy in the cell
how does the cell membrane decide what enters or leaves

solution_steps.explain: The selectively permeable membrane encloses the cytoplasm.
The nucleus holds chromosomes carrying genetic instructions.
Mitochondria power, ribosomes build proteins, and vacuoles store.

concepts.title: Observing Cells with Microscopes and Scales
concepts.definition: Cells lie far below naked-eye reach, so light microscopes in school laboratories reveal them, and scale ladders - from a kilometre down to a human height, a chicken egg, a fish egg, most plant and animal cells, bacteria and viruses - place each biological object at its true size.
concepts.key_idea: Microscope plus a size ladder: cells are small, viruses smaller, and scales make it exact.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc102.txt microscope observation and scale sections
question_patterns: why are microscopes needed to study cells

solution_steps.explain: Light microscopes enlarge thin specimens for viewing.
Compare sizes from kilometres to ribosomes to grasp the scale of life.
Sketch and label what the microscope reveals.
